c:840.name: United States (federal)
c:840.rules_effective: Marijuana remains Schedule I under the federal CSA, so there are no federal marijuana product standards. Hemp falls under the 2018 Farm Bill (7 U.S.C. 1639o) and USDA 7 CFR Part 990, which regulate only THC compliance of the crop. FDA regulates finished hemp/CBD products only through the general FD&C Act adulteration provisions; no CBD-specific contaminant limits exist.
c:840.pending_changes: P.L. 119-37 (FY2026 Agriculture Appropriations, Div. B; enacted 11/12/2025) redefines hemp. The crop uses a total-THC basis below 0.3% dry weight. Final hemp-derived cannabinoid products are capped at 0.4 mg total THC per container. Products containing cannabinoids the plant cannot naturally produce, or naturally occurring cannabinoids that were synthesized or made outside the plant, are excluded from hemp. FDA was directed to publish cannabinoid lists and to define 'container'. The change was originally effective 11/12/2026; the continuing resolution H.R. 6500 (September 2026) delays it about one month, to roughly 12/11–12/12/2026 (press reports disagree on the exact date). Any federal rescheduling of marijuana to Schedule III would still not set product contaminant limits.
sources: CRS Insight IN12620 — Change to Federal Definition of Hemp
RCRC — CR delays hemp THC restrictions (Sept 4, 2026)
Bloomberg Government — Hemp ban delay passed (Sept 1, 2026)
